pharm: Purified human menopausal gonadotrophin containing follicle-stimulating and luteinising hormone activity, used to stimulate follicular development and ovulation in assisted reproduction.
quick: Individualised; commonly start 75-150 IU SC/IM daily, titrated
Contraindicated (used to achieve, not during, pregnancy)
Ovarian ultrasound, serum estradiol, signs of OHSS
summary: Menotrophin (human menopausal gonadotrophin, hMG) is a purified preparation from the urine of postmenopausal women containing both FSH and LH activity. It is used under specialist supervision to induce follicular development for ovulation induction in anovulatory infertility and for controlled ovarian stimulation in assisted reproductive technology (e.g. IVF). Treatment requires close monitoring (ultrasound and estradiol) to time ovulation triggering and to detect ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) and reduce multiple pregnancy. It is not approved by the US FDA under this exact name but is available in the EU/elsewhere.
indications: Induction of ovulation in women with anovulatory infertility not due to primary ovarian failure
Controlled ovarian stimulation to develop multiple follicles for assisted reproductive technology (e.g. IVF/ICSI)
Stimulation of spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism (with hCG, specialist use)

dosage.d: Start 75-150 IU daily; adjust by no more than 37.5-75 IU at intervals of at least 7 days based on response
dosage.n: Give hCG to trigger ovulation once a mature follicle develops; withhold if over-response

dosage.d: Typically 150-225 IU daily from early follicular phase, individualised; max usually about 450 IU/day
dosage.n: Continue until adequate follicular development, then trigger with hCG

dosage.d: Commonly 75-150 IU three times weekly with hCG (specialist regimen)
dosage.n: Used after hCG-induced testosterone normalisation; long-term

admin: Reconstitute the powder gently with the supplied diluent immediately before use; do not shake vigorously
Administer by subcutaneous or intramuscular injection as directed; rotate injection sites for SC use
Use only under specialist supervision with cycle monitoring (ultrasound and hormone levels)
Time the ovulation-triggering hCG dose precisely as instructed; abstain or have timed intercourse/insemination per plan
Withhold hCG and avoid intercourse if there is excessive ovarian response to reduce OHSS and multiple-pregnancy risk
moa: Menotrophin supplies exogenous follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinising hormone (LH) activity. FSH drives growth and maturation of ovarian follicles and stimulates granulosa-cell estradiol production; LH activity supports follicular steroidogenesis and, with the subsequent hCG trigger that mimics the LH surge, promotes final follicular maturation and ovulation. In men, the FSH/LH activity (with hCG) stimulates Sertoli and Leydig cell function to support spermatogenesis.

absolute: Primary ovarian failure / high FSH indicating gonadal failure
Uncontrolled non-gonadal endocrine disorders (thyroid, adrenal, pituitary)
Hormone-dependent tumours of the ovary, uterus, breast (women) or testis/prostate (men)
Tumours of the hypothalamus or pituitary
Ovarian cysts or enlargement not due to polycystic ovary syndrome
relative: Prior poor or exaggerated ovarian response
monitor: Ovarian response by ultrasound and serum estradiol
Signs and symptoms of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome

preg: Contraindicated during pregnancy; menotrophin is used to achieve pregnancy, not during it. Once pregnancy occurs, discontinue. Multiple pregnancy and its complications are recognised risks of treatment.
lact: Not indicated during breastfeeding; fertility treatment is not undertaken while lactating.
renal: No specific dosing data; use under specialist supervision. Eliminated partly renally.
hepatic: No specific dosing data; use under specialist supervision.

moderate: Clomifene citrate (additive ovarian stimulation; may increase follicular response)
GnRH agonists/antagonists (used together in controlled protocols; alter required gonadotrophin dose)
minor: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic drug interactions established
interactions.diagnostics: May affect interpretation of gonadotrophin and estradiol assays during monitoring.

emergency: Severe OHSS (rapid weight gain, severe abdominal pain, breathlessness, reduced urine output)

monitoring: Symptoms/signs of OHSS and body weight
Pregnancy outcome and number of gestational sacs
counsel: This treatment is closely monitored with scans and blood tests to time your trigger injection
Report severe or rapidly worsening abdominal pain, bloating, breathlessness, or reduced urination - signs of overstimulation
Be aware of the increased chance of twins or higher-order pregnancy
Use the injection technique and timing exactly as taught by your fertility team
Seek urgent care for leg swelling/pain or chest pain
pk: Follicular growth develops over days of daily dosing
Serum gonadotrophin peaks within hours of injection
Cumulative effect over a stimulation cycle (days)
Refrigerate or store per product label; protect from light; use reconstituted solution immediately
pearls: Specialist-only fertility drug; requires ultrasound and estradiol monitoring to time the hCG trigger
Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is the key serious risk - withhold hCG and reassess if over-response
Counsel on the increased risk of multiple pregnancy
missed: Dosing is managed by your fertility specialist on a daily schedule. If you miss or are late with a dose, contact your clinic for instructions rather than adjusting the dose yourself - do not double up.
overdose: Overdose is most likely to result in ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome rather than acute toxicity. Management is supportive: monitor for OHSS (fluid shifts, haemoconcentration, electrolyte disturbance), maintain fluid/electrolyte balance, prevent thromboembolism, and withhold the hCG trigger.
